headline: Leaving Pine Knot
summary: After the Thanksgiving holiday at Pine Knot in Albemarle County, Virginia, Roosevelt heads back to Washington in the evening.

events.detail: Returns to Washington in the evening

headline: Army-Navy game and three water projects
summary: On his and Edith's 19th wedding anniversary, Roosevelt watches Army play Navy at Princeton. The same day brings three new federal reclamation projects: Rio Grande and Carlsbad in New Mexico and Okanogan in Washington.

events.detail: Rio Grande, Carlsbad and Okanogan reclamation projects established

headline: Sunday evening callers
summary: At 9 p.m. Roosevelt receives Robert Bacon, William Willcox, Elbert Baldwin, Mrs. John Van Voorst and a Mr. Quellenec.

headline: The 59th Congress opens
summary: The 59th Congress gathers. Roosevelt talks New York politics with Olcott and that evening sees Chief Justice Fuller, Justice Holmes and Alexander Graham Bell. The Umatilla project in Oregon is approved, and TR tells Moody wood pulp should carry no tariff.

events.detail: Evening with Fuller, Holmes, Bell and others
Writes Moody on the wood pulp duty

letters.topic: Wood pulp ought to come in duty-free

headline: A tougher Annual Message
summary: Roosevelt sends Congress his fifth Annual Message, a more forceful document pressing for railroad rate regulation and pure food laws. He also holds Cabinet, lunches with Brooks Adams, and sees Minister Takahira at night; Nicholas Murray Butler is a White House guest.

events.detail: Fifth Annual Message urges rail rate and pure food laws
Senators Pettus, Allison, Long and Morgan and Representative Williams stop in

references.title: Theodore Roosevelt, the Paradox of Progressivism

headline: A gift of Sully's Memoirs
summary: Roosevelt thanks Paul d'Estournelles de Constant for an early printing of the Duke of Sully's memoirs, a gift from the French government in gratitude for his help keeping peace with Germany. He also confers on Brooklyn patronage and on health in the Philippines with Dr. Gorgas, and dines with Lodge, Nick Longworth and others.

events.detail: Brooklyn appointments with Woodruff and Payne
Lunches with the Winthrops, Takahira and Richard Saltonstall
Visits from Senators Smoot, Frye, Clapp, Spooner and Flint and Representative Crumpacker
Dinner with Hengelmüller, Hale, Lodge, Longworth and Wetmore
Thanks d'Estournelles de Constant for the French gift

letters.topic: Gratitude for France's gift of Sully's Memoirs

uncertain: Governor Winthrop identified as Beekman Winthrop of Puerto Rico; first names of several senators inferred.

headline: Saving the golden trout
summary: Roosevelt writes David Starr Jordan about the golden trout named for him, a fish he had worked to protect. He tells Selous how much the family enjoyed his visit and demands that Charles McClelland account for his insurance dealings.

events.detail: New York appointments with Platt and R. C. Morris
Sees Cockran, Fairbanks, and Senators Gallinger, Teller and Foraker
Letters to Selous, McClelland and Jordan

letters.topic: Warm thanks for his stay
Asks him to explain his insurance conduct
The Roosevelt golden trout

tr_quotes.text: If you enjoyed your visit to the White House half as much as we enjoyed having you, I am more than content.

headline: A marshal's badge for a Rough Rider
summary: After Cabinet and a tariff talk, Roosevelt writes Senator Clarence Clark about naming Ben Daniels, a former Rough Rider and Western lawman, as a U.S. marshal. A musicale fills the evening.

events.detail: Cabinet meeting; tariff talk with Dingley

letters.topic: Wants Rough Rider Ben Daniels made a U.S. marshal

uncertain: The record says TR wanted 'Clark' appointed, but the context points to Daniels. 'Dingley' is not further identified (Nelson Dingley had died in 1899).

headline: Seth Bullock comes to lunch
summary: Roosevelt confers with Beveridge on statehood, then sits down to lunch with two old Western friends, Seth Bullock and William Llewellyn, plus General Thomas and Nick Longworth. Booker T. Washington calls at 9 p.m., followed by Moody, Brownlow and Hale.

events.detail: Lunch with Bullock, Llewellyn, Thomas and Longworth
Visits from Felix Adler and E. P. Bacon

headline: William Barnes calls
summary: Sunday evening callers at the White House include New York Republican William Barnes.

headline: Ultimatum to the Storers
summary: In separate letters to Bellamy and Maria Storer, Roosevelt ends their meddling in Vatican affairs: they must stop writing Rome on Catholic matters and misrepresenting U.S. policy, or Bellamy loses his post as ambassador in Vienna. TR also meets labor leaders Mitchell and Gompers on Chinese exclusion.

events.detail: Chicago appointments with C. E. Smith
Chinese exclusion with Mitchell, Gompers, Easley and others
Separate warnings to Bellamy and Maria Storer

letters.topic: Stop Vatican lobbying or be removed from Vienna
Stop Vatican lobbying or her husband loses his post

uncertain: C. E. Smith identified tentatively as Charles Emory Smith.

headline: Carnegie and the Yakima project
summary: The Yakima reclamation project in Washington is approved. After Cabinet, Roosevelt discusses insurance legislation with Representative Landis and meets William Sulzer and immigration inspector Marcus Braun; Andrew Carnegie is among his callers.

events.detail: Visits from Carnegie, Crane, Dolliver and Yates

headline: Dinner with Charles Freer
summary: Roosevelt discusses irrigation with Senators Smoot and Sutherland and canal business with Joseph Bishop. Nick's mother, Mrs. Longworth, comes to lunch, and art collector Charles Freer dines with the Lodges, the Holmeses and Mrs. Gardner.

events.detail: Irrigation with Smoot and Sutherland; canal matters with Bishop
Senators Penrose, Aldrich, Wetmore, Heyburn and Long and Speaker Cannon call
Dinner with Freer, the Lodges, the Holmeses and Mrs. Gardner

uncertain: "Mrs. Longworth" taken to be Nick's mother, Susan Longworth; Mrs. Gardner not further identified.

headline: Alice's engagement made public
summary: The White House announces that Alice will marry Congressman Nicholas Longworth of Cincinnati on February 17, 1906. Roosevelt also writes Lyman Abbott about how party politics is tangling both the rate bill and the Dominican treaty, and Jacob Schiff about Russian Jews.

events.detail: Philippine tariff with W. F. Wakeman
Engagement of Alice and Nick Longworth announced

letters.topic: Party politics clouding the rate bill and Dominican treaty
The plight of Jews in Russia

headline: A customs post for Bill Sewall
summary: Roosevelt proposes his old Maine guide Bill Sewall for a customs collectorship, thanks the Provençal poet Frédéric Mistral for a copy of Mirèio, and writes Moody denying any shielding of Paul Morton in the Equitable affair. The Strawberry Valley project in Utah is approved.

events.detail: California patronage with Senators Perkins and Flint
Discusses the insurance inquiry with Representative Alexander and R. L. Cox
Letters to Mistral, Powers and Moody

letters.topic: Thanks for the gift of his poem Mirèio
Suggests Bill Sewall as a Maine customs collector
The Equitable case and claims he protected Morton

uncertain: Representative Alexander's first name inferred.

headline: Snowball fights behind the White House
summary: Snow falls, and Archie, Quentin, cousin Sheffield Cowles and Helen Elliott go sledding and pelt each other with snowballs behind the White House. Roosevelt's article "Federal Social Legislation" appears in Charities and the Commons, and he confers on Santo Domingo and the canal.

events.detail: Santo Domingo with Spooner; canal bills with Hepburn and Hale
Children sled and snowball in the snow

headline: Sunday supper with Major Wadsworth
summary: At 7:30 Roosevelt sups with Major W. A. Wadsworth, and later sees Senators Allison and Hale, Theodore Shonts and Joseph Bishop.

events.detail: Sees Allison, Hale, Shonts and Bishop

headline: Urging Selous to write
summary: Roosevelt meets Senator Kittredge, Shonts, Moody and Taft about pay for canal workers, and lunches with editor Richard Watson Gilder. He urges Frederick Selous to put his big-game knowledge into a book.

events.detail: Canal salaries with Taft, Moody, Shonts and Kittredge
A pension agent post with Gallinger, Proctor and Dillingham
Lunches with Gilder, Scott and Dunn
Urges Selous to write a big-game book

letters.topic: Encourages him to write about big game

headline: A gift for his childhood nurse
summary: Roosevelt sends a $20 check, by way of Corinne, to Dora "Dolly" Watkins, his nurse as a boy. Joseph Bishop is named to the Canal Commission, and TR writes a stack of letters, thanking Admiral Togo for a revolver and denying he called Argentines superior to other South Americans.

events.detail: Seth Bullock, Landis and W. W. Cocks call
Bishop appointed to the Canal Commission
Goes to a play staged by the Army and Navy League
Letters to Watkins, Hughes, Fuller, Abbott, Root, Dunn and Togo

letters.topic: A $20 gift sent through Corinne
McClelland's improper conduct
Freer's collection gift to the Smithsonian
Press attacks on Lodge as a Massachusetts boss
Denies an Argentine report about his remarks
Backing Wadsworth for Assembly Speaker
Thanks for a revolver

headline: A win over Odell
summary: Roosevelt tells Herbert Parsons that Wadsworth has been picked over Merritt for New York Assembly Speaker, a setback for Odell. He asks Bonaparte to circulate an article on the Russo-Japanese naval fighting so it can shape U.S. ship design.

events.detail: Canal bills with Kittredge and Aldrich; Delaware with Allee

letters.topic: Wadsworth's selection for Speaker over Merritt
Spread lessons of the Russo-Japanese sea battle to guide U.S. warship design

uncertain: The record dates the naval battle 1904; the major fleet action, Tsushima, was in 1905.

headline: Cabinet dinner as Congress recesses
summary: Congress breaks for the holidays, and Roosevelt hosts a Cabinet dinner; Eliot Gregory and Paul Morton stay the night. He tells Shonts a Mr. Sullivan is wrong to think William Cromwell ever had his confidence, and writes Secretary Wilson on saving Western grazing lands.

events.detail: Cabinet dinner; Gregory and Morton stay overnight
Letters to Shonts and James Wilson

letters.topic: Denies Cromwell ever had his trust
Protecting grazing land in the West

tr_quotes.text: that is interesting and just what I would expect. But Mr. Sullivan is mistaken about Mr. Cromwell having had my confidence!

headline: Hide-and-seek with the children
summary: Roosevelt and the children chase one another through the mansion in a game of hide-and-seek. He talks Wyoming forest reserves with Senator Warren, sees Whitelaw Reid, and goes with Edith to a dinner in their honor given by Vice President Fairbanks.

events.detail: Fairbanks dinner for TR and Edith

headline: Dinner with the Hoosier poet
summary: Roosevelt confers on Brooklyn patronage and canal business, lunches with the Fairbankses and two Japanese visitors, Commander Takeshita and Mr. Kitagaki, and dines with James Whitcomb Riley and the Vice President.

events.detail: Brooklyn appointments with Dady; meetings with Bishop and Hepburn
Lunch with the Fairbankses, Whitcomb, Takeshita and Kitagaki

uncertain: "J. W. Riley" read as poet James Whitcomb Riley; the lunch guest "Whitcomb" may be the same man.

headline: Christmas Eve callers
summary: On Christmas Eve, Roosevelt discusses New York politics with James Wadsworth Jr. and Commissioner Cooley, then sees Ambassador Jusserand and later Francis Leupp.

events.detail: New York politics with Wadsworth and Cooley

headline: Christmas at the White House
summary: The Roosevelts spend Christmas Day in Washington.

headline: Overruling Lucius Swift
summary: Roosevelt meets Root, Taft and Bonaparte in the afternoon. He tells Indiana reformer Lucius Swift that he will name Rothschild, Senator Beveridge's choice, surveyor of customs despite Swift's objections.

events.detail: Afternoon meeting with Root, Taft and Bonaparte
Letter to Swift on the customs appointment

letters.topic: Will appoint Rothschild Indiana's customs surveyor over Swift's protest

headline: Off to Pine Knot for the holidays
summary: Roosevelt receives Peru's new minister at 10 a.m., then leaves with the family for Pine Knot, their cabin in Albemarle County, Virginia.

events.detail: Leaves with the family for Pine Knot

headline: At Pine Knot
summary: The Roosevelts are at Pine Knot in the Virginia countryside; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Another day at Pine Knot
summary: The family remains at Pine Knot; no events are noted.

headline: Steunenberg assassinated in Idaho
summary: While Roosevelt is at Pine Knot, Harry Orchard, a Western Federation of Miners man, kills former Idaho Governor Frank Steunenberg.

headline: Home to Washington
summary: Roosevelt returns to Washington and sees Senator Eugene Hale at 10 p.m.

headline: New Year's reception
summary: Roosevelt greets the public at the White House New Year's reception from late morning into early afternoon, and sees British Ambassador Durand that night. He praises Charles Larned's article on the Army, which called for better pay.

letters.topic: Admires his article urging higher military pay

headline: Wadsworth wins the Speakership
summary: Roosevelt wires Herbert Parsons to stand firm for James Wadsworth against Hamilton Fish's man, Wainwright. Wadsworth becomes Speaker of the New York Assembly, a clear victory for TR. The day also brings Cabinet and a stream of senators.

events.detail: Six senators drop by, along with canal men Bishop and John Stevens

letters.topic: Hold firm for Wadsworth against Fish's candidate

headline: Advice to a new Speaker
summary: Roosevelt talks statehood with Beveridge and confers with Grosvenor, then attends a Cabinet dinner at Secretary Root's. He sends counsel to James Wadsworth on his new job and writes Governor Higgins about Odell.

events.detail: Visits from Cannon, Spooner, Hepburn, Burkett, Lacey and Hinshaw
Letters to Higgins, Wadsworth and Hale

letters.topic: Odell and the Speakership fight
Guidance for the new Assembly Speaker
The Panama Canal Commission

headline: The Hepburn rate bill goes in
summary: Congress returns, and Representative Hepburn's railroad rate bill is put before the House. Roosevelt's lunch table includes Herbert Parsons, Lloyd Griscom, Butler, Reid and Speck von Sternberg, and hosts the diplomatic reception that night.

events.detail: Congress reconvenes; Hepburn bill introduced in the House
Lunch with Sternberg, Reid, Butler, Griscom, Parsons and others

headline: Lunch with Mr. Dooley's creator
summary: Humorist Finley Peter Dunne joins Roosevelt for lunch with Taft, Root, Jusserand and others. That evening TR takes up the Naval Personnel Bill with four Cabinet members; Butler stays over.

events.detail: An Indianapolis appointment with Beveridge and Overstreet
Lunch with Dunne, Taft, Root, Jusserand, Young, Stevens and others
Evening meeting on the Naval Personnel Bill

uncertain: "Stevens" taken to be canal engineer John F. Stevens; "Young" not identified.

headline: The coinage is his pet project
summary: Roosevelt tells Augustus Saint-Gaudens that the new coinage is a project close to his heart and that he dislikes the Mint's objections to the designs. He also discusses canal labor with Shonts and J. B. Harris, Black appointments with Charles Anderson, and sees Alexander Graham Bell.

events.detail: Canal labor with Shonts and Harris
Appointments of Black officials with Anderson
Letter to Saint-Gaudens on the coins

letters.topic: His devotion to the coin project and annoyance at the Mint

headline: Stimson for the trust cases
summary: Roosevelt writes Senator Platt that he wants Henry L. Stimson named district attorney to prosecute the American Sugar Refining Company and the New York Central Railroad under the Elkins Act.

letters.topic: Wants Stimson to prosecute the sugar trust and New York Central

headline: A special message on the canal
summary: Roosevelt sends Congress a special message on the Panama Canal and receives the American Bar Association's commission. He writes Leonard Wood with concern over a head wound, asks John Pitcher whether John Goff was mauled by a lion, and tells Luke Wright he wants him as Minister to Japan.

events.detail: Receives the American Bar Association commission
Cabinet officers and several members of Congress call
Sends lawmakers a message devoted to Panama
Letters to Wood, Pitcher, Wright and Lowell

letters.topic: Worry over Wood's head injury
Was John Goff attacked by a lion?
Aoki replaces Takahira; asks Wright to go to Tokyo
The foreign service and its people

works.title: Special message to Congress on the Panama Canal

headline: No third term
summary: Roosevelt gives Lincoln Steffens free rein to investigate the executive branch. Writing Jeter Pritchard, he denies any shift toward a whites-only Republican policy in the South and flatly rules out a third term.

events.detail: Grants Steffens open access to investigate the executive departments
Secretary Shaw gives a dinner for TR and Edith
Letter to Pritchard on Southern policy and a third term

letters.topic: Denies a white-supremacy turn in the South; refuses a third term

tr_quotes.text: useless to talk to me of accepting a third term. Under no consideration would I do so.

headline: A Medal of Honor at the White House
summary: Roosevelt pins the Medal of Honor on James Robb Church, the first such award handed out at the White House under the formal ceremony TR had ordered. He also makes Henry Stimson the federal prosecutor in Manhattan and addresses the American Medical Association.

events.detail: Hands the nation's highest military award to Church
Names Stimson U.S. Attorney in New York

letters.topic: Schiff's speech and the money question

works.title: Address to the American Medical Association

uncertain: Edwin Denby identified from "Denby".

headline: Diplomatic dinner
summary: Roosevelt hears Dominican property holders on the Santo Domingo treaty and discusses the Philippine tariff bill with E. J. Hill. The White House hosts a diplomatic dinner, and he writes Root on Venezuela and Taft on Army camps and the Chinese boycott.

events.detail: Hears from owners of property in the Dominican Republic about the treaty
Spooner, Long and Representative Bell call

letters.topic: Venezuela
Army summer camps; Chinese boycotts and riots

headline: Schiff hurt, not helped
summary: After Cabinet and a talk with Watson about tariffs on Philippine goods, Roosevelt writes Butler again about Jacob Schiff's January 4 speech attacking U.S. finance policy, which he thinks did harm.

letters.topic: Schiff's critique of federal fiscal policy

tr_quotes.text: Schiff, so far from helping, distinctly hurt the situation.

headline: A lock canal, and gifts for Alice
summary: Roosevelt writes Kermit that he favors a lock canal over a sea-level one at Panama, that he often rides and walks with Edith, and that wedding gifts for Alice are starting to come in. He sends along a pin given him by Oklahoma ranchmen.

events.detail: Meets Stevens and Bishop; Hepburn bill with Esch and Hepburn
Root, Fairbanks, Millard and Beveridge call
Dinner for New York Republicans and Cabinet officers

letters.topic: A ranchmen's pin, lock canal, rides with Edith, Alice's gifts

tr_quotes.text: The wedding presents have begun to arrive for Sister.

headline: Meeting New York's postmaster
summary: Roosevelt confers with William Willcox, postmaster of New York.

headline: Jane Addams and Steffens drop in
summary: Roosevelt discusses New York politics with Herbert Parsons and the canal inquiry with Senator Kittredge. Among a crowd of visitors are reformers Jane Addams and Lincoln Steffens.

events.detail: New York politics with Parsons; canal probe with Kittredge
Meetings with Shonts, Cortelyou, Taft, Reid, Aldrich, Fulton, Millard, Edwards, Addams and Steffens

headline: Algeciras opens; Perdicaris visits
summary: The Algeciras Conference on the Franco-German quarrel over Morocco opens in Spain, a meeting Roosevelt helped arrange, with Henry White there to guide it. That afternoon Ion Perdicaris, the kidnap victim of 1904, calls with his wife. The House passes the Philippine tariff bill.

events.detail: Alaska governorship with Lodge, Allison, Piles, Ryan and Swineford
Visit from Ion Perdicaris and his wife
Algeciras Conference convenes with Henry White representing the U.S.
House passes the Philippine tariff bill
Taft's dinner for TR and Edith
Writes Moody about George Walker for Indian Territory attorney

letters.topic: Naming George Walker U.S. Attorney for Indian Territory

headline: Sevier National Forest created
summary: Roosevelt establishes the Sevier National Forest in Utah. In a packed day he confers on Alaska, railroad rates and the Hague Conference and lunches with Taft and Herbert Parsons.

events.detail: Alaska with Lodge and Piles; rates with Elkins; the Hague with Bartholdt
The Speaker and several lawmakers call

headline: Arizona and New Mexico as one
summary: On Bamie's 51st birthday, Roosevelt tells Benjamin Ide Wheeler he hopes to bring the Arizona and New Mexico territories in together as a single state, since separate admission would take years. He meets Spooner on the Dominican treaty and a Puerto Rico delegation, and hosts the judiciary reception.

events.detail: Santo Domingo treaty with Spooner; a Puerto Rican delegation
A long line of officials and lawmakers call
LaFarge and cousin John Roosevelt are overnight guests
Letter to Wheeler on joint statehood

letters.topic: Favors admitting Arizona and New Mexico jointly

uncertain: "J. E. Roosevelt" taken to be cousin John Ellis Roosevelt.

headline: Luke Wright to Tokyo
summary: Roosevelt appoints Luke E. Wright U.S. ambassador to Japan after a Cabinet meeting. His brother-in-law Douglas Robinson is staying at the White House.

events.detail: Brother-in-law Robinson is a house guest

headline: Dewey and the senators
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senator Elkins on rate legislation, and separately with Admiral Dewey, Senators Frye and Spooner and Representative McCall. Root, Hitchcock and Alger also call.

events.detail: Meeting with Dewey, Frye, Spooner and McCall

headline: Brooklyn patronage and Steffens
summary: On a Sunday, Roosevelt talks Brooklyn appointments with Timothy Woodruff, and Lincoln Steffens stops by.

headline: The comfort of books
summary: Roosevelt asks the Army's General Staff whether a war plan against Venezuela should be drafted and urges Leonard Wood to think about fortifying Hawaii given Japan's ambitions. To Trevelyan he writes that liking every sort of book is a great comfort and that reading rests him from work.

events.detail: Portuguese workers for Hawaii with Atkinson; New Jersey postal reform with Mayor Fagan
Statehood with Watson; New York politics with Black
Letters to the General Staff, Wood and Trevelyan

letters.topic: Whether to prepare a campaign plan for Venezuela
Defending Hawaii against possible Japanese expansion
Reading as rest; Soapey Sponge's Sporting Tour

tr_quotes.text: I find it a great comfort to like all kinds of books.

headline: Against coolie labor
summary: After Cabinet and a meeting with Speaker Cannon and Representative Humphrey, Roosevelt writes Whitelaw Reid that he opposes bringing Chinese coolie labor into the United States. Attorney General Moody gives a dinner for TR and Edith.

events.detail: Letter to Reid on coolie labor

letters.topic: Opposes importing Chinese contract laborers

headline: Praise for Jane Addams
summary: Roosevelt receives China's imperial commissioners and talks Far Eastern matters with Paul Morton. He tells Jane Addams he admires her kind of reformer, writes Leupp about coal lands on Choctaw and Chickasaw reservations, and defends the Hague Conference to Ian Hamilton.

events.detail: Visits from Foster, Overman and Shaw
Letters to Leupp, Hamilton and Addams

letters.topic: Coal lands on Choctaw and Chickasaw reservations
Soldiers raised in town versus country; defends the Hague meeting
Admiration for her brand of reform

headline: Dinner for the Supreme Court
summary: Roosevelt works the statehood bill with a number of congressmen, lunches with Bowdoin president William DeWitt Hyde, and gives the justices of the Supreme Court an evening dinner.

events.detail: Statehood bill with many members of Congress

uncertain: W. D. Hyde identified as William DeWitt Hyde.

headline: Bribes in the Beef Trust case
summary: Roosevelt writes Moody about bribes the meatpackers used to try to influence the government's Beef Trust prosecution and Senator Aldrich about tribal funds going to church-run Indian schools. He meets on trade with Asia and hosts a 32-guest dinner; Hugo Münsterberg calls.

events.detail: Asian commerce with Metcalf, McLaurin and Overman

letters.topic: Packers' bribery aimed at the Beef Trust prosecution
Tribal money for sectarian Indian schools

headline: A Gridiron Club evening
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Dryden and Governor Stokes, sees C. E. Smith and Overstreet, and goes to the Gridiron Club's dinner at the Willard Hotel. He tells Ted he is glad his Harvard work has improved.

events.detail: Lunches with New Jersey's Governor Stokes and John Dryden
C. E. Smith and Overstreet call
Off-the-record remarks at the Gridiron Club on sensational journalism

letters.topic: His improving grades at Harvard

works.title: Gridiron Club remarks on the muck-rake

uncertain: The record places the muck-rake remarks here; TR's Gridiron Club muck-rake talk is dated March 17, 1906, and he repeated it in public on April 14.

headline: Explaining the muck-rake speech to Steffens
summary: With canal money, the Hepburn rate bill, the Philippine tariff, the Dominican treaty and joint statehood all pending in Congress, Roosevelt sees Senator La Follette at 9:30 p.m. and then Lincoln Steffens, to whom he explains the thinking behind his Gridiron remarks.

events.detail: Gives Steffens the background to the muck-rake remarks

headline: Fighting Joe Wheeler's funeral
summary: Roosevelt goes to General Joseph Wheeler's funeral, confers with Representative Keifer, and hosts an evening musicale.

headline: Riis comes to stay
summary: Roosevelt confers with Governor Charles Magoon on Panama and sees Lincoln Steffens again. Jacob Riis is a White House guest, and Secretary Cortelyou gives a dinner for TR and Edith. He tells French Chadwick a new President and Congress ought to take office together at New Year's.

events.detail: Letter to Chadwick on inauguration timing

letters.topic: President and Congress should start their terms together on January 1

tr_quotes.text: new President and the new Congress should go into office together on the first of the New Year.

headline: Pearls, tapestries and popcorn
summary: Gifts pour in for Alice and Nick: a Gobelin tapestry from France's president, embroidered gold cloth from Japan's emperor, a $25,000 pearl necklace from Cuba, a Saint-Gaudens bronze, an Italian mosaic table and a hogshead of popcorn. Alice turns nothing down. The Senate begins to move on the Hepburn bill.

events.detail: Talks over Puerto Rican affairs with Todd and Larrinaga
Lunches with Riis, Root and Bonaparte
Cannon, Beveridge, Alger and Penrose call
Letter to Senator Long backing the rate bill
Wedding presents arrive from around the world
Senate takes up the Hepburn bill

letters.topic: His support for the railroad rate bill

headline: Reinstating a midshipman
summary: Roosevelt tells Representative George Foss he is letting Midshipman John Paul Miller return to the Naval Academy, though hazing ordinarily meant automatic dismissal. He also writes Meyer about French jitters over German demands at Algeciras and confers on rate legislation and Wisconsin patronage.

events.detail: Rate legislation with Dolliver and Clapp; Wisconsin jobs with La Follette and Spooner

letters.topic: French anxiety over German demands at Algeciras
Reinstates Midshipman Miller despite the hazing charge

headline: A ride with Edith
summary: Roosevelt and Edith go riding. He discusses Government Printing Office business with Representative Landis, and Douglas and Corinne Robinson stay at the White House for a dinner and musicale.

events.detail: Government Printing Office matters with Landis

headline: Harvard '80 at the White House
summary: Roosevelt hosts a dinner for his Harvard Class of 1880. Ted arrives from college and rides with his father, who writes Kermit about David Copperfield and his fondness for Thackeray. He presses the Storers for answers to his December letters.

events.detail: Ted arrives from Harvard and rides with his father
Hosts his college classmates for dinner
Letters to Bellamy Storer, Kermit and Taft

letters.topic: Demands replies to his December 11 letters
Thoughts on David Copperfield and Thackeray; Ted's visit
Respect for enlisted men's uniforms

headline: Kermit's amber beads
summary: Edith writes Kermit that Alice wears the amber beads he sent as a wedding present constantly; he had paid $50 for them at Fisher's.

events.detail: Edith writes Kermit about Alice and his gift

headline: A report on the Pennsylvania Railroad
summary: The Interstate Commerce Commission's report on alleged antitrust violations by the Pennsylvania Railroad goes to the House. Taft, Speaker Cannon and three senators call on Roosevelt.

events.detail: ICC report on the Pennsylvania Railroad sent to the House
Senators, the Speaker and Taft call

headline: Lunch with John Burroughs
summary: Roosevelt lunches with naturalists John Burroughs and C. Hart Merriam and Major John Pitcher. A letter of his to Congress on Annapolis hazing is made public, and he complains to Steffens that the Senate killed the Santo Domingo treaty along party lines.

events.detail: His letter to Congress on hazing laws is released
Lunch with Burroughs, Merriam and Pitcher
Bonaparte's dinner for TR and Edith

letters.topic: His removal of Idaho's William McConnell as Indian inspector
Partisan defeat of the Dominican treaty in the Senate

works.title: Letter to Congress on hazing at the Naval Academy

headline: Artillery and the rate bill
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Dr. Alexander Lambert and Secretary Metcalf and dines with Robert Wynne. He writes Senator Knox backing better training for coast and field artillery and urging that the rate bill become law.

letters.topic: Artillery training and the rate bill

headline: The House passes the Hepburn bill
summary: The House of Representatives approves the Hepburn railroad rate bill, a key piece of Roosevelt's program. He also meets House naval committee members about hazing at Annapolis, hosts the Army-Navy reception, and writes Francis Heney about corruption in San Francisco.

events.detail: Discusses Annapolis hazing with House naval committee members

letters.topic: Graft in San Francisco

headline: Ray Stannard Baker at lunchtime
summary: Roosevelt sees journalist Ray Stannard Baker at 12:45, confers with Senators Depew and Platt and editor Edward Butler on Buffalo jobs and on rates with Elkins, and gives a dinner for the Republican National Executive Committee.

events.detail: Buffalo jobs with Platt, Depew and Butler; rates with Elkins
Dinner for the Republican National Executive Committee

headline: Indian Key bird reservation
summary: Roosevelt creates the Indian Key bird reservation in Florida. He meets a National Businessmen's League delegation, sees Jusserand, and warns Bonaparte and Taft that ammunition stocks would fall short in a war.

events.detail: Letters to Bonaparte and Taft on ammunition shortages

letters.topic: Insufficient ammunition reserves for wartime
Insufficient ammunition reserves for wartime

headline: Sunday night senators
summary: Senators John Spooner and George Nixon call on Roosevelt at 9 p.m.

headline: Alice turns 22; Bill Sewall at lunch
summary: On Alice's 22nd birthday, Roosevelt lunches with his old Maine guide Bill Sewall, Guy Murchie and Taft, and the White House throws a dinner and musicale in her honor. In a lengthy letter to John St. Loe Strachey he covers presidential power and free trade and describes Nick as a fine fellow and Harvard's best violinist.

headline: Relief for famine-struck Japan
summary: Roosevelt calls on Americans to help the people of Japan, then suffering a famine. He spends part of the day lunching and walking with John Burroughs, and tells Dr. Lambert he cannot write Wadsworth and Higgins about legislation.

events.detail: Cabinet meeting; naval expansion with Foss
Lunch and a walk with Burroughs

headline: Alice marries Nick Longworth
summary: At noon on a clear, mild day, Alice Roosevelt, 22, marries Congressman Nicholas Longworth, 36, in the East Room before roughly 700 guests, with no bridesmaids. Her Lee grandparents are there, as are Sara Delano Roosevelt and young Franklin. Afterward Alice hugs Edith, and the couple leave to honeymoon in Cuba.

headline: Hold the Hepburn bill as written
summary: Roosevelt sees Lincoln Steffens in the morning and Speck von Sternberg at 6, and dines with Lodge. He tells Pennsylvania Railroad president Alexander Cassatt he wants the Hepburn bill passed unamended, and presses for stricter medical screening of immigrants arriving at Ellis Island. In Chicago, Taft argues for a standing army.
